newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN SUGAR FIRMS AS FESTIVAL DEMAND SHOWS.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN SUGAR FIRMS AS FESTIVAL DEMAND SHOWS.

text.p: Sugar prices firmed on local Indian markets as increased consumer buying ahead of festivals showed up in a thin market, dealers said.
In ready delivery sugar S-30 rose five rupees to 1,485/1,515 rupees per quintal while sugar M-30 rose eight to 13 rupees to 1,511/1,550.
Sugar for mill delivery remained subdued amid absence of outstation buying but offerings by millers also remained low.
Mill delivery sugar S-30 slid 10 rupees to 1,415/1,420 rupees, while sugar M-30 fell by same margin to 1,430/1,450.
Expectations of growing festival demand buoyed sentiment.
"The state governments have improved the quantum of sugar supplied through public distribution system but this sugar was reported to be of inferior quality," one broker said.
"Consumers have to depend on the open market for superior varieties for the festivals," he said.
